text:
carmen: quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposal to add a lightweight 'shadow allocator' to enable deterministic replay of allocation/eviction order for frag-induced OOMs. thoughts?
ben: this sounds super useful for triage. curious about overhead and privacy across tenants.
priya: also curious how it interacts with offload/evictor ordering. if we replay allocations but eviction timings change, is the bug still reproducible?
kai: implementation sketch: record allocation events (addr, size, alloc_id, stackid) + eviction decisions (evict_id, victim_addr, timestamp) into a circular ring buffer. sample vs full capture modes.
carmen: yes — two modes: sample (1/1000 allocations) for low overhead, and full-capture for repro runs (triggered via tenant header or testing job). replay can be fed into a deterministic simulator that replays: allocations -> simulated eviction policy -> observe fragmentation.
ben: what about KV cache and prefix caching? those mutate residency outside normal alloc/free. need to capture logical cache touch events.
priya: +1. we should capture higher-level ops (kvcache.touch key, kvcache.evict key) rather than raw memcpy events so replay maps to policy decisions.
kai: tradeoffs: full capture will be heavy for high-throughput hosts. we can compress events on the fly (delta timestamps, use varint) and drop payloads. also rotate to S3 for postmortem analysis.
carmen: infra/privacy: for multi-tenant, full capture may include pointers that could be correlated to user data. plan: obfuscate pointers and avoid recording payloads; treat stackids as local integers. require tenant opt-in for full-capture. default sample-only and metrics-derived traces are safe.
priya: how do ops team trigger a full capture? admin API? or automatic when OOM occurs?
kai: two paths: (1) automatic snapshot-on-oom: when we predict imminent OOM (resident > threshold) start a short full-capture window (10s) and persist, (2) manual via debug header + job id.
ben: automated snapshot on OOM is great for reproducibility. My concern: race conditions where replay differs because kernel scheduling or GPU command queue timings differ. we need to freeze external inputs and replay deterministically in a simulator, not live.
carmen: exactly — replay run won't run on live GPUs. we build a deterministic simulator that models allocator logic, evictor heuristics, and offload latency distributions. We feed recorded events and check if the simulated fragmentation path leads to OOM.
priya: does that mean we must version allocator/evictor code used for simulation? otherwise replay drift.
kai: yes, record serving runtime version + policy flags with each capture. the simulator will use matching code branch or best-effort shim. store the commit sha in the trace metadata.
ben: UX: we should expose a small CLI: rdebug analyze <trace_id> --run-sim to produce a compact diagnosis: hot-slab churn %, largest free block over time, predicted vs observed eviction counts.
carmen: example capture header for sample mode:```json
{"trace_id":"t-999124-01","mode":"sample","sample_rate":1000,"runtime_sha":"abc123"}
```
priya: Nice. For the ring buffer format, please keep line-delimited JSON events so ad-hoc grep/awk works. schema: {evt:"alloc", id:123, size:65536, stack:55, t:512345}.
kai: perf note: do not allocate during capture path. pre-allocated buffers + mmap a file for the ring buffer. write is atomic append with seqnum.
ben: ops: retention policy? traces could be large. propose keep sample traces 30d, auto-capture-on-oom retained 90d, manual kept until explicit delete.
carmen: acceptance criteria for rollout: (1) can reproduce 3 historical fragmentation incidents in sandbox with simulator, (2) overhead in sample mode < 1% p95 tail, (3) privacy opt-in enforced for full capture.
priya: implementation plan + owners? I can take simulator and analysis tooling. kai can do runtime capture and ring buffer. ben can handle infra + storage + retention. carmen will drive integration and rollout.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: can create feature branch template: branch/feature/shadow-alloc-replay, CI job skeleton + perf test harness. :white_check_mark:
carmen: next steps: PR sketch + design doc for the ring-buffer format. I'll draft the doc and ping reviewers. if anyone has strong objections to capture semantics or privacy constraints speak up now.
ben: no objections. add opt-out annotation for enterprise tenants that cannot allow any tracing.
priya: add a simple opt-in flag in tenant settings and audit logging for captures.
kai: I'll add a small prototype in a debug build to validate overhead numbers. posting a short perf script in thread when ready.
carmen: thanks all — will put a short RFC follow-up with open questions. we should avoid calling it 'shadow allocator' in public docs; internal codename fine. :+1:
